title: Restoration Fee Bands by Days Since the Missed Due Date — Northgate Card Past-Due Accounts
content:
| Days since the missed due date | Standing late fee | Restoration fee |
|---|---|---|
| 30 or more | above zero | every late fee recorded on the account in the last two months less the fee reversals posted in that time, never less than zero |
| 1 to 29 | above zero | the standing late fee |
| 0 (today is the due date or earlier) | any | none |
| any | zero | none |

On a past-due **Northgate Card Credit Accounts (issued by Harbor Point Bank, N.A.)** account the restoration fee follows the days since the missed due date and the standing late fee: where 30 or more days have passed and the standing late fee is above zero, it is every late fee recorded on the account in the last two months less the fee reversals posted in that time, never less than zero, a month counted back from today to the same calendar day; where 1 to 29 days have passed and the standing late fee is above zero, it is the standing late fee; in every other case there is none.

**Terms.** The missed statement is the statement for which the most recent late fee on the account was recorded, and of two late fees posted the same day the one entered first in the account history. The standing late fee is the late fee recorded for the missed statement less every reversal already posted against it, never less than zero. The days since the missed due date are the calendar days from the missed statement's payment due date to today. The fee reversals posted in the last two months are all fee reversals on the account in that time.

**Hypothetical boundaries (missed due date on the 1st of a 30-day month).** On the 30th, 29 days have passed: the standing late fee. On the 1st of the next month, 30 days have passed: the two-month total. Late fees of 32.00 and 43.00 recorded in the last two months with a 10.00 reversal in that time give 65.00; a fee dated on the same calendar day two months back is outside the two months.
